html:
Tres Molinos (“Three Mills”) is a small town in a gorge in Selezia, where Alvaro da Silva and Fernan arrive in chapter 32 to investigate what happened to the philosopher van Halm. An overnight train from Laerta reaches the station, a hundred miles from Seleza; in the morning, after coffee, the passenger gets off.

The town (ch. 32)

The narrator ironically describes Tres Molinos as “the dullest of backwaters”: three hundred and twenty inhabitants, a town hall with a clock, running water, an inn called Comfortable Rooms, taverns called Breakfasts in Boxes and the Holy Torero, and a shop called Odds and Ends. The three windmills that gave the town its name do not grind wheat—there is none in rice-growing Selezia—but pump water into the water tower’s tank. Locals navigate by three directions: “near the temple,” meaning the temple of the Ancient Lords a mile south, closed shortly after the First Judge; “up above,” meaning the House Above, an old castle on the plateau; and “over there,” meaning everywhere else. After the temple closed, the locals say, the region stopped developing.

The characters get to know the town through two guides: Javier Salam, nicknamed “Need Anything?” (Javier Salam), and the coffeehouse owner Senora Marques, whose “museum of misfortunes” consists of stories of disasters connected with the castle.

The castle and its curse (ch. 32–34)

The town has long talked about the castle’s curse: its victims include the former owner Nivendey and van Halm himself. The climb to the castle and Alvaro’s investigation are described in chapter 34; there Alvaro also observes that the water tower stands lower than the castle and calls this one of the two facts everyone else overlooked. See Last Winter and The Night at Last Winter.
